newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN FORD PLANT DENIES LOSING VAN OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN FORD PLANT DENIES LOSING VAN OUTPUT.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Belgian factory on Monday denied reports that the U.S. car maker might move assembly of its Transit vans from the Belgian town of Genk to Southampton in England.
"We will continue to build the current Transit and certainly build the new model, its successor," Ford Genk director Peter Heller told Reuters.

Belgian daily De Standaard said on Saturday that the BBTK socialist union had a Ford document that led it to the conclusion that assembly could be moved to England within the next few years to concentrate the activity in one plant.
But Heller said Ford's headquarters had reconfirmed that Genk would continue to assemble Transits. "I've just informed our workers," he added.
He declined to say when the new model was due to be launched but said it would not be this year.
Ford Genk currently employs 11,500 people. About 2,500 people produce Transits. The others assemble the Mondeo saloon car and handle spare parts for other plants.
The plant in Genk, northeastern Belgium, built some 380,000 Mondeo saloon cars and about 70,000 Transits in 1996.
It is the lead plant for the Transit, which is also produced in Southampton and in Portugal.
The report came at a time when Belgian politicians and unions are up in arms over a unilateral decision by French car maker Renault to close its Belgian assembly plant by July.
The closure will cost 3,100 Renault workers and some 1,000 workers at suppliers and subcontractors their jobs.
Genk, a division of Ford's German unit Ford Werke AG, exports 96.5 percent of its production and accounts for 40 percent of total car exports from Belgium.
